item.title: Misting Monsoon Diving opens Destin location for boat maintenance services
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Misting Monsoon Diving, a Tampa Bay-based underwater services company, has opened its newest location in downtown Destin, bringing specialized hull cleaning and marine inspection services to the Emerald Coast. Founded by Jarrett Maryon, a PADI Advanced Master Diver with nine years of experience, the company focuses on underwater maintenance work…
item.content:encoded:
Misting Monsoon Diving, a Tampa Bay-based underwater services company, has opened its newest location in downtown Destin, bringing specialized hull cleaning and marine inspection services to the Emerald Coast.

Founded by Jarrett Maryon, a PADI Advanced Master Diver with nine years of experience, the company focuses on underwater maintenance work including hull cleaning, zinc replacement, propeller services, and underwater inspections. The new Destin operation will serve boat owners across the area, including marinas and private docks along Destin Harbor, Choctawhatchee Bay, and Santa Rosa Sound, as well as surrounding communities like Fort Walton Beach and Niceville.

To mark its arrival, Misting Monsoon is offering local boat owners a complimentary zinc inspection and $50 off zinc replacement services. The company emphasizes a commitment to environmental stewardship, noting that its Tampa Bay team has participated in underwater cleanup efforts removing hundreds of pounds of debris from local waterways—a practice it plans to continue in the Emerald Coast area.

Interested boat owners can reach the Destin location at 850-750-2207 or visit destin.mistingmonsoon.com.

item.title: ALDOT Plans Traffic Island at I-10/US 98 Exit in Daphne
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Alabama Department of Transportation is planning to install a traffic island at the westbound I-10 exit in Daphne that would block drivers from continuing straight toward the Causeway bypass, according to WPMI NBC 15. The change would require drivers to turn either left or right onto U.S. 98 instead of proceeding directly. The project has…
item.content:encoded:
The Alabama Department of Transportation is planning to install a traffic island at the westbound I-10 exit in Daphne that would block drivers from continuing straight toward the Causeway bypass, according to WPMI NBC 15. The change would require drivers to turn either left or right onto U.S. 98 instead of proceeding directly.

The project has already drawn concerns from the community and local officials who worry about the impact on traffic flow and driver confusion during the transition. The specifics of ALDOT's timeline and reasoning for the modification were not immediately detailed in the station's initial reporting.

This area handles significant traffic, particularly during peak commute times and when drivers are using the Causeway to cross the bay. More details about the project scope and expected completion date were not yet available.

item.title: Pensacola residents push back on proposal to limit public comment at city council
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Residents speaking before the Pensacola City Council have voiced concerns about a potential move to restrict public comment periods to city business topics only, warning that the measure could limit an important avenue for civic engagement. According to reporting on the matter, residents emphasized that public comment at council meetings…
item.content:encoded:
Residents speaking before the Pensacola City Council have voiced concerns about a potential move to restrict public comment periods to city business topics only, warning that the measure could limit an important avenue for civic engagement.

According to reporting on the matter, residents emphasized that public comment at council meetings represents one of the few direct channels they have to communicate with elected officials between election cycles. Several speakers argued that narrowing the scope of permissible remarks would undermine transparency and reduce opportunities for constituents to raise concerns about broader community issues.

The council did not take action on any changes to its public comment rules during the meeting, leaving the current procedures in place for now. The debate reflects an ongoing tension in many municipalities between maintaining structured agendas and preserving open forums for resident input.

item.content:encoded: Proposed changes to the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) could significantly increase demand at food pantries across the region, according to NBC 15. The changes would reduce benefits for eligible recipients, potentially forcing more families to seek assistance from local charities and community organizations. Baldwin County food pantry officials say they're preparing for a possible surge in clients if the federal cuts move forward. The timing comes as holiday food needs typically peak in late fall and winter, potentially compounding the strain on already stretched resources.

item.title: Cambridge Dictionary picks 'human' as 2026 word of the year amid AI concerns
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Cambridge Dictionary has selected "human" as its word of the year for 2026, a choice reflecting growing cultural anxieties about artificial intelligence and its role in society. The selection marks a notable turn back to a word with roots stretching to the 15th century, underscoring what lexicographers see as a defining concern of our moment.…
item.content:encoded:
The Cambridge Dictionary has selected "human" as its word of the year for 2026, a choice reflecting growing cultural anxieties about artificial intelligence and its role in society. The selection marks a notable turn back to a word with roots stretching to the 15th century, underscoring what lexicographers see as a defining concern of our moment.

According to WKRG-TV 5, the decision to highlight "human" reflects broader conversations about what it means to be distinctly human in an era of rapid AI advancement. The choice suggests a cultural moment where people are reassessing fundamental values and identity in the face of technological change.

Word-of-the-year selections by major dictionaries often serve as cultural snapshots, capturing the preoccupations and conversations dominating public discourse during a given year.

item.title: Baptist Health Care Celebrates First Medical Assistant Training Program Graduates
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Baptist Health Care marked a milestone this week with the graduation of its first cohort from an in-house medical assistant training program, an effort designed to develop career pathways for existing staff while addressing workforce shortages in a growing field. Five employees—Briana Jones, Madison Murphy, Kylie Tavener, Shane Vose-Mora, and…
item.content:encoded:
Baptist Health Care marked a milestone this week with the graduation of its first cohort from an in-house medical assistant training program, an effort designed to develop career pathways for existing staff while addressing workforce shortages in a growing field.

Five employees—Briana Jones, Madison Murphy, Kylie Tavener, Shane Vose-Mora, and Danika Wray—completed the 20-week curriculum, which runs concurrently with their regular jobs and includes 80 hours of clinical externship and certification exam preparation. The inaugural class began in May 2026. Medical assistants support physicians and care teams in clinical and office settings, handling patient intake, vital signs, basic lab work, and administrative tasks.

Baptist said demand for certified medical assistants is climbing both locally and nationally. The program is open to Baptist employees with a high school diploma in good standing, and graduates must commit to working as a certified medical assistant within Baptist for at least two years. The organization has already shifted to a rolling enrollment model, selecting two participants every other month with a goal of graduating about 12 annually. Cohorts are set to begin in November and January, with more slots opening throughout 2027.

Many graduates go on to pursue advanced credentials as licensed practical nurses, registered nurses, or other allied health professionals, Baptist said. The program reflects the health system's broader strategy as one of the region's largest private employers.

item.title: Rep. Salzman hosting Thanksgiving food distribution for 400+ families Saturday
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The drive-through event begins at 7:30 a.m., with vehicles welcome to line up starting at 6:00 a.m. A minimum of 400…
item.content:encoded:
State Representative Michelle Salzman and Jennifer Harrison will distribute 30,000 pounds of food to families in need this Saturday at Marcus Pointe Baptist Church in Pensacola, according to a press release from Salzman's office.

The drive-through event begins at 7:30 a.m., with vehicles welcome to line up starting at 6:00 a.m. A minimum of 400 families will receive assistance while supplies last. Each household will get two boxes: one with a week's worth of food essentials and another with complete Thanksgiving dinner fixings. Limited quantities of baby food, diapers, and wipes will also be available.

"This event reflects the power of partnerships and our shared commitment to serving our community during the holidays," Salzman said in the release. "We want to ensure that every family has food on the table and the resources to enjoy a warm Thanksgiving meal together."

The effort is a collaboration between Salzman's office, Feeding the Gulf Coast, and numerous community partners including the Escambia County Sheriff's Office, Florida Power & Light, International Paper, and local businesses. For volunteer information, contact Jennifer Harrison at 850-324-2744.

item.title: HUD to Screen FHA Mortgage Applicants for Delinquent Child Support
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development announced Wednesday a new automated system to prevent people with unpaid child support from obtaining federally-insured mortgages. Starting March 18, 2027, lenders processing FHA-insured loans will be required to screen applicants through the Treasury Department's "Do Not Pay" portal to identify…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development announced Wednesday a new automated system to prevent people with unpaid child support from obtaining federally-insured mortgages. Starting March 18, 2027, lenders processing FHA-insured loans will be required to screen applicants through the Treasury Department's "Do Not Pay" portal to identify those with delinquent child support obligations.

Federal law already prohibits providing FHA-insured mortgages to borrowers with delinquent child support, but the new system marks the first direct connection between HUD's FHA Connection technology and Treasury's screening database. The automated process will flag ineligible applicants without requiring borrowers to submit additional paperwork or register with new systems.

HUD Secretary Turner said the measure protects taxpayers and enforces existing law. "If you owe delinquent child support, you should not receive a taxpayer-backed mortgage," Turner said in a statement. The screening applies to anyone subject to federal administrative offset due to unpaid child support obligations.

item.title: Alabama Closes Public Oyster Season After Just 12 Harvest Days
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: State officials say oyster populations have fallen sharply, with this year's harvest expected to be a fraction of previous years. MOBILE, Ala. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Alabama's public oyster harvesting season is coming to an unusually early end as state marine officials report another sharp decline in the number of oysters available for commercial…
item.content:encoded:
State officials say oyster populations have fallen sharply, with this year's harvest expected to be a fraction of previous years.

MOBILE, Ala. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Alabama's public oyster harvesting season is coming to an unusually early end as state marine officials report another sharp decline in the number of oysters available for commercial harvesting.

The Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources announced that all public oyster reefs would close to harvesting at 2 p.m. Wednesday, November 18.

The closure ends a season that provided commercial harvesters with just 12 working days.

By comparison, Alabama's public oyster harvesting season lasted 54 days in 2025 and 58 days in 2024.

Oyster Harvest Falls Dramatically

State officials estimate this year's commercial oyster harvest will total fewer than 400 sacks.

That's a dramatic decline from approximately 5,000 sacks harvested in 2025 and nearly 25,000 sacks in 2024.

Surveys conducted before the season found low numbers of harvestable oysters in three areas:

  • Heron Bay

  • Cedar Point West

  • Cedar Point East

Those results prompted the state to limit harvesting opportunities when the season opened November 2.

Marine Resources Division officials say the continued decline reflects several years of difficult environmental conditions affecting Alabama's coastal waters.

Poor Water Conditions Hamper Recovery

According to state marine biologists, fluctuations in salinity and periods of low dissolved oxygen have harmed oyster populations.

Those conditions can interfere with reproduction, reduce survival rates among young oysters and slow their growth.

Marine Resources Division Director Kevin Anson said surveys showed fewer oysters of harvestable size than researchers had estimated during the previous year.

Officials also found a decline in the number of young oysters, raising additional concerns about the population's ability to recover.

Anson said oysters require at least 18 months to reach harvestable size, meaning favorable water conditions would need to persist for an extended period before populations could substantially rebound.

Protecting Remaining Oyster Populations

State officials say closing public reefs early is intended to protect the remaining spawning population.

Allowing those oysters to reproduce is considered essential to rebuilding the resource and supporting future commercial harvesting.

The Marine Resources Division is continuing to work with Auburn University researchers to study oyster reproduction and water quality in Mobile Bay and Mississippi Sound.

That work includes research aimed at identifying the best locations for oyster reef restoration.

The effort is supported by funding from the Deepwater Horizon oil spill settlement.

For Alabama's commercial oyster industry, the abbreviated season underscores the challenges facing one of the Gulf Coast's longstanding fisheries.

item.title: Court Documents Reveal New Details in Foley Attempted Kidnapping
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Investigators say a 13-year-old boy escaped after suspects armed with a rifle tried to force him into a vehicle. FOLEY, Ala. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Newly filed court documents are providing additional details about an attempted kidnapping in Foley that resulted in seven arrests over the weekend. According to court records obtained by FOX10 News, a…
item.content:encoded:
Investigators say a 13-year-old boy escaped after suspects armed with a rifle tried to force him into a vehicle.

FOLEY, Ala. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Newly filed court documents are providing additional details about an attempted kidnapping in Foley that resulted in seven arrests over the weekend.

According to court records obtained by FOX10 News, a 13-year-old boy was grabbed and dragged toward a vehicle at gunpoint outside a convenience store on Highway 59 early Sunday morning.

The boy managed to escape before the suspects could force him into the vehicle.

Seven people between the ages of 13 and 19 have been arrested in connection with the investigation.

Attempted Abduction Outside Convenience Store

The incident occurred during the early morning hours of November 15.

Foley Police initially received a report shortly before 4 a.m. involving two groups of young people acting suspiciously in a parking lot along Highway 59.

Investigators later determined that members of one group allegedly attempted to abduct someone from the other group.

According to a Baldwin County District Court complaint, three teenagers confronted a 13-year-old boy outside a Circle K convenience store.

The complaint alleges that the suspects produced a black AR-style rifle, grabbed the boy and dragged him toward a black sedan.

The boy escaped before he could be taken away.

The court documents do not specify which suspect was holding the rifle.

Seven Arrested in Joint Investigation

Foley Police worked with the Baldwin County Sheriff's Office to identify and arrest those believed to be involved.

One of the defendants, 19-year-old Johnnie Joel Duarte-Olarte, has been charged with attempted first-degree kidnapping.

Authorities say charges against the seven suspects range from attempted kidnapping and burglary to menacing and firearms offenses.

Two of those arrested were expected to face attempted first-degree kidnapping charges.

Investigators also recovered several firearms during the arrests, including one reported stolen.

A separate court complaint charges an 18-year-old woman with burglary and a firearms offense in connection with the broader investigation.

Police Say No Ongoing Public Threat

Foley Police Chief Kevin Carnley has said investigators have not found evidence indicating the incident was gang-related.

Authorities also say they do not currently believe there is an ongoing threat to the public.

Investigators are continuing to examine the relationship between the two groups and the circumstances leading up to the attempted abduction.

The case remains under investigation.

All defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

item.title: UWF marks major milestone with final beam placement at Darrell Gooden Stadium
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida celebrated a significant construction milestone today with a topping out ceremony for Darrell Gooden Stadium, placing the final structural beam in what will become the home of the university's Division I football program. Campus community members and supporters signed the final steel beam before construction crews…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida celebrated a significant construction milestone today with a topping out ceremony for Darrell Gooden Stadium, placing the final structural beam in what will become the home of the university's Division I football program.

Campus community members and supporters signed the final steel beam before construction crews lifted it into place, a tradition the university says honors both the structural achievement and the workers who made it possible. An evergreen tree was placed on the beam, following a longstanding construction custom symbolizing growth, good fortune, and successful framework completion. "Everyone who signed their name on the final steel beam cemented themselves in the UWF history books, forever becoming a part of Darrell Gooden Stadium," UWF President Manny Diaz Jr. said in a statement.

The stadium project broke ground in February 2026 and has advanced rapidly. The facility will span more than 62,400 square feet with 7,205 seats and a total capacity exceeding 10,000. A state-of-the-art LED video board was installed over the summer to enhance the game-day experience. Work continues on the stadium tower, north and south buildings, and bleachers, with interior finishes, tower windows, and seating planned for spring 2027. Lighting, concourse structures, and canopies will follow in summer 2027.

Darrell Gooden Stadium is scheduled to open in fall 2027, marking the beginning of Argonaut football in the new facility and reflecting UWF's continued investment in its Division I athletics program.

Las Vegas resort charges and high-value vehicle purchases are often among the first red flags that trigger audits and investigations.

The case remains active in the local federal court system. More information is expected to be released as the case progresses.

item.title: Sacred Heart Earns Another Top Hospital Safety Grade
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Ascension Sacred Heart Pensacola has earned another top rating for patient safety, receiving an A in the Leapfrog Group's fall 2026 Hospital Safety Grades. According to the hospital, Sacred Heart was the only hospital in the Pensacola area to earn an A in the latest evaluation. The recognition marks the…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Ascension Sacred Heart Pensacola has earned another top rating for patient safety, receiving an A in the Leapfrog Group's fall 2026 Hospital Safety Grades.

According to the hospital, Sacred Heart was the only hospital in the Pensacola area to earn an A in the latest evaluation.

The recognition marks the hospital's 11th A grade in the last 12 grading periods, spanning approximately six years.

The Leapfrog Group is an independent national nonprofit organization that evaluates hospitals based on their performance in preventing medical errors, infections, injuries and other patient safety problems.

Hospitals are assigned letter grades ranging from A to F, with evaluations released twice a year.

What the Rating Measures

The Leapfrog Hospital Safety Grade examines more than 22 measures related to patient safety.

Those measures include how effectively hospitals prevent infections, avoid medical mistakes and maintain systems designed to protect patients from preventable harm.

The evaluations also consider hospital practices intended to reduce complications and improve the overall safety of patient care.

Unlike hospital rankings that examine a broad range of services, Leapfrog's ratings focus specifically on patient safety.

Hospital Credits Caregivers

Sacred Heart President and CEO Rick Metzger credited the hospital's employees for maintaining the facility's record of high safety grades.

In announcing the recognition, Metzger said the rating reflects the work of the hospital's caregivers and their commitment to providing safe, high-quality care.

The hospital says its clinical teams regularly work toward patient safety goals involving infection prevention, improved procedures and the identification of potential risks.

The latest A grade continues a lengthy period of favorable evaluations for the Pensacola hospital.

Ascension Sacred Heart previously received an A in the spring 2026 grading period.

Information for Patients

The Leapfrog Group publishes its hospital safety grades online, allowing patients to review individual hospitals and compare their performance on various safety measures.

The organization says its goal is to provide consumers with information that can help them make more informed healthcare decisions.

Patients can review hospital ratings and additional safety information at HospitalSafetyGrade.org.

item.title: Florida Dems Elect Two Haitian Americans to Legislative Leadership Posts
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Senate and House Democratic Caucuses this week elevated two Haitian American legislators to top party positions, according to the Florida Democratic Party. Senator Mack Bernard was elected Senate Democratic Leader Pro Tempore, while Representative Marie Woodson was tapped as House Democratic Leader Pro Tempore — a move party chair…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Senate and House Democratic Caucuses this week elevated two Haitian American legislators to top party positions, according to the Florida Democratic Party. Senator Mack Bernard was elected Senate Democratic Leader Pro Tempore, while Representative Marie Woodson was tapped as House Democratic Leader Pro Tempore — a move party chair Nikki Fried called a significant milestone for Haitian American representation in the state legislature.

Bernard and Woodson's elections reflect the growing political influence of Florida's Haitian American community, which has become a key voting bloc in the state. Fried noted both lawmakers have focused their careers on issues including affordable housing, healthcare access, and educational opportunity.

"Florida's Haitian American community has helped shape our state in countless ways, and its leadership deserves to be reflected in the halls of power," Fried said in a statement released Wednesday. The elevation of Bernard and Woodson to leadership roles marks one of the first times both legislative chambers have simultaneously had Haitian American lawmakers in top Democratic positions.

item.title: Todd Thomson Steps Down as Greater Pensacola Chamber CEO After 8 Years
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Todd Thomson is wrapping up his tenure as President and CEO of the Greater Pensacola Chamber of Commerce at year's end, concluding more than a decade with the organization overall. Thomson took on the role in an interim capacity in February 2019 and was officially named President that April. During his eight years leading the Chamber, he navigated…
item.content:encoded:
Todd Thomson is wrapping up his tenure as President and CEO of the Greater Pensacola Chamber of Commerce at year's end, concluding more than a decade with the organization overall.

Thomson took on the role in an interim capacity in February 2019 and was officially named President that April. During his eight years leading the Chamber, he navigated the organization through significant regional challenges, including the COVID-19 pandemic and multiple hurricanes. He became a key point of contact for local businesses seeking reliable information during those crises, launching the "From the President's Desk" eblast—initially a daily digest of pandemic resources that evolved into a weekly roundup for members.

The Chamber's board chair, Ildi Hosman, praised Thomson's steady leadership through turbulent times. "During the pandemic and the hurricanes, our members knew they could count on him for clear information and a direct line to decisionmakers," Hosman said in a statement. Thomson also represented the business community as part of Escambia County's Emergency Support Function 18 during Hurricane Sally and Hurricane Isaias.

Beyond crisis management, Thomson elevated the Chamber's voice on local issues ranging from development of Outlying Field-8 to tax policy and opposition to expanded Gulf oil and gas drilling. He launched the Chamber Connection radio show, a podcast series, and quarterly "State of" luncheons featuring leaders in education, health care, the military, and the economy. Thomson originally joined the Chamber in 2015 as Vice President of Public Affairs, where he built the Chamber's advocacy program and deepened ties with local government.

item.title: UWF Celebrates Major Construction Milestone at Darrell Gooden Stadium
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: University officials and community supporters gathered Wednesday as the new stadium reached a significant step toward its planned 2027 opening. PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — The University of West Florida celebrated a major construction milestone Wednesday morning as work continues on Darrell Gooden Stadium, the future home of Argonaut…
item.content:encoded:
University officials and community supporters gathered Wednesday as the new stadium reached a significant step toward its planned 2027 opening.

PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — The University of West Florida celebrated a major construction milestone Wednesday morning as work continues on Darrell Gooden Stadium, the future home of Argonaut football.

The university held a topping-out ceremony at PenAir Field, marking the placement of the final structural beam in the stadium's framework. Hundreds of supporters were expected to attend the event, with participants invited to sign the beam before it was raised into position.

UWF Athletic Director Dave Scott spoke with NewsRadio 92.3's Chris Bryan Wednesday morning as preparations for the ceremony were underway.

Scott said the stadium's transformation has become increasingly noticeable in recent days as the structure rises above the existing football field.

"I gotta admit, I mean between this and the last game, just seeing the structure really take place. This is pretty cool," Scott said.


From 4,000 Seats to a 10,000-Person Stadium

The transformation will substantially increase the university's ability to accommodate football fans and other events.

Scott said the current configuration provides seating for approximately 4,000 spectators, with existing bleachers concentrated on one side of the field.

Once completed, Darrell Gooden Stadium will accommodate approximately 10,000 people, including 7,500 seats and several premium seating options.

The stadium's new multilevel structure will include:

  • A field-level club accommodating approximately 200 guests, with a drink rail overlooking the playing field.

  • The PenAir Champions Club, providing space for approximately 400 guests and featuring two bars.

  • Twelve luxury suites accommodating between eight and thirty guests each.

  • Six additional suites on the upper level.

  • New coaching, radio broadcasting and public-address facilities.

  • Expanded concessions, locker rooms and spectator seating extending from goal line to goal line.

Scott said work on the stadium's western structure will continue through the spring and summer, ahead of the facility's scheduled opening for the 2027 football season.


Season Ticket Sales Planned for Spring

With UWF making its transition into NCAA Division I athletics, the expanded stadium will provide additional opportunities for fans to attend games on campus.

Scott said the university expects to begin its season ticket process in the spring, with priority initially given to existing donors and season ticket holders.

Sales are expected to open to the general public sometime around April or May.

The stadium project represents a significant investment in UWF athletics. Construction began in February following a lead donation of more than $9 million from philanthropist Darrell Gooden, for whom the stadium is named.

The project also received $2 million in funding through Escambia County's Tourist Development Council.

UWF expects the stadium to serve as a venue for football, university activities and other community events.

Argonauts Look Ahead

While stadium construction continues, the Argonauts are preparing to conclude their first Division I football season.

UWF is scheduled to face West Georgia this weekend in a matchup the university is calling the "Borderline Brawl."

Scott also highlighted the university's fall athletic programs, including the women's volleyball team's appearance in the ASUN Championship.

The university is also looking ahead to its Battle of the Bay basketball matchup with Florida State University at the Pensacola Bay Center following Thanksgiving.

Darrell Gooden Stadium is expected to welcome fans for its first full season in fall 2027.
